stories.headline: Federal Government Prepares to Table 2026 Budget Focusing on Affordability
stories.summary: Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne is set to table the Liberal government's second budget under Prime Minister Mark Carney. The spending plan is expected to prioritize cost-of-living relief, a $36-billion business tax break, and updated immigration targets. Ottawa aims to position the economy against global volatility while navigating an ongoing trade war.

stories.headline: Canadian Leaders and Industry Weigh Potential Tariff Relief Following U.S. Midterms
stories.summary: The U.S. Democratic Party swept both chambers of Congress in midterm elections, prompting Canadian political leaders and aluminum producers to express optimism for relief from cross-border tariffs. While Ontario Premier Doug Ford and other provincial premiers welcomed the outcome as a rebuke of President Donald Trump's trade agenda, federal officials remain cautious and emphasize that plans to diversify trade will persist. Cross-border trade negotiations continue as the Trump administration retains executive authority over trade measures.

stories.headline: Doug Ford Rejects New Long-Term Funding Deal for Toronto Budget Shortfall
stories.summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford has ruled out negotiating a "New Deal 2.0" to resolve the City of Toronto's projected $1.12-billion budget deficit. While dismissing a formal long-term financial agreement with Mayor Olivia Chow, Ford indicated Queen's Park remains open to providing some provincial funding earmarked for public safety.

stories.headline: Ontario Liberal Leadership Candidates Spar Over Taxes in Final Debate
stories.summary: Candidates for the Ontario Liberal Party leadership made their final pitches to members ahead of voting, framing themselves as the solution to Premier Doug Ford's government. Contenders Navdeep Bains and Stephanie Bowman pledged tax freezes, while competitors Lee Fairclough and Dylan Marando advocated for broader tax reform.

stories.headline: Court Certifies Class Action Over COVID-19 Negligence at Downsview Long-Term Care
stories.summary: The Ontario Superior Court has certified a class-action lawsuit against Downsview Long-Term Care Centre and its parent company, Gem Health Care Group. The lawsuit alleges that gross negligence in the home's response to the COVID-19 pandemic led to lethal outbreaks and hundreds of resident deaths. The defendants consented to the class action certification.

stories.headline: Ontario Doctors Demand Apology Over Ministry Letters Questioning Days Worked
stories.summary: The Ontario Medical Association and family physicians are demanding an apology after the provincial health ministry sent letters questioning doctors for working high numbers of days and seeing excessive patient volumes. Physicians criticized the communications as intimidating amidst existing doctor shortages, while the Ministry of Health maintained the notices did not allege improper billing.

stories.headline: Ontario to Expedite OSAP Review for Low-Risk Private Career Colleges
stories.summary: Premier Doug Ford announced that third-party auditors reviewing student financial aid will prioritize clearing low-risk private career colleges to unfreeze their access to funding. All Ontario career colleges currently face an OSAP funding freeze following an investigation into potential aid fraud. The province has not yet provided a definitive timeline for when the audits will conclude.

stories.headline: Doug Ford Signals Openness to Ending Seasonal Time Changes With Regional Alignment
stories.summary: Premier Doug Ford stated that Ontario is open to permanently ending seasonal time changes if neighbouring Quebec and adjacent eastern U.S. jurisdictions agree to make the shift. Moving to permanent daylight time would require coordinated regional legislation, though critics note it could result in darker winter mornings.

stories.headline: Canada and China Extend Trade Agreement on Agricultural Goods and Metals
stories.summary: Ottawa and Beijing have agreed to extend tariff-free access for Canadian agricultural exports, including canola, lobster, and crab, until late 2028. In exchange, Canada will maintain market access for Chinese steel and aluminum shipments. The two-year extension aligns with federal objectives to significantly expand Canadian exports to the Chinese market.

stories.headline: National Watchdog Warns Canadian Military Online Surveillance Poses Privacy Risks
stories.summary: A report from Canada's national intelligence watchdog warns that Canadian Armed Forces policies fail to adequately address privacy risks when conducting online surveillance. The review found that current military rules do not sufficiently govern the collection of domestic information on Canadian citizens gathered through internet searches.

stories.headline: Early Childhood Educators Protest Ontario Wage Freeze at Queen's Park
stories.summary: Early childhood educators gathered at the Ontario legislature to protest a provincial memo freezing their wage floor and eliminating a scheduled one-dollar hourly wage increase for 2027. Workers criticized the Ford government's compensation cap as detrimental to child-care staffing, while parent fees remain capped under provincial agreements.

articles.title: Early childhood educators call out Ontario over wage freeze, while child care capped at $22 until 2027

stories.headline: Amazon GTA Workers Launch Union Organizing Campaign With Unifor
stories.summary: Amazon warehouse employees in the Greater Toronto Area launched a unionization campaign at a rally in Scarborough in partnership with Unifor. The organizing drive seeks to unionize workers across multiple regional fulfillment centres to improve workplace representation.

articles.title: Amazon workers in Toronto area launch organizing drive with help of Unifor

stories.headline: Mikisew Cree Nation Challenges Pacific Link Pipeline in Federal Court
stories.summary: The Mikisew Cree Nation has filed a legal challenge in Federal Court against the federal government's Pacific Link pipeline project. The Indigenous community contends that Ottawa failed to fulfill its legal obligation to consult them before approving the infrastructure development.

articles.title: Le projet d’oléoduc Pacific Link contesté en Cour fédérale par la Nation crie Mikisew

stories.headline: Majority of GTA Residents Support Relocating Encampments to Facilities
stories.summary: A new poll indicates that more than 80 per cent of residents across Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area support moving individuals from public encampments to supervised support facilities. A large majority endorsed relocation even if such measures infringed on individuals' legal rights.

articles.title: Poll finds majority in Toronto, GTA want people moved from encampments to support facilities
